    The factor by which the escapes that follow model-placed ignitions differ from the observed ones

    chainedEscapeFactor.Rd

    When fireSense_burn places ignitions with the ignition model, each ignition escapes with the escape model's probability at the pixel it lands in (fireSenseUtils::escapeProbPerIgnition()), and the expected escapes of the fit period are sum(w * lambda * q) over the pixel-years (w the share in the core, exposureOf(), lambda the expected ignitions of the whole pixel, q the escape probability per ignition), from the in-sample fold-mean predictions that fittedYearEffects() starts from. c is the observed escapes over these.

    chainedEscapeFactor(ignitions, escapes)

    Arguments

    ignitions

    data.table of the ignition fit data, one row per pixel and year, as for fittedYearEffects(): pixelID, year, observed (ignitions), mean (predicted ignitions of the whole pixel) and weight (its share in the core).

    escapes

    data.table of the escape fit data for the same pixel-years: pixelID, year, observed (escapes) and mean (the predicted escapes if ignited).

    Value

    A list: c, ignitionRatio, escapeCalibration, placement, qObserved, qModel, and the totals observedIgnitions, expectedIgnitions, observedEscapes, expectedEscapes (c = observedEscapes / expectedEscapes).

    Details

    c is the structural level, WITHOUT year effects: lambda and the escape mean are the models' predictions as they are (multiplier 1), not multiplied by the fitted year multipliers. Those are relative to this level, and fittedYearEffects() solves the escape multipliers on the ignitions already scaled by the ignition multipliers, which is a different quantity from c. The weights are fireSense_burn's rule: it draws Poisson ignitions (drawCounts()) with the whole pixel's mean on every coarse pixel, escapes each with q (drawEscapes(), rbinom(ignitions, q)), places each ignition in a random flammable cell of its coarse pixel and keeps the starts in the core (inELFCore()), so a pixel's expected core ignitions are coreFraction * lambda and its expected core escapes coreFraction * lambda * q, as here.

    It is split exactly into three factors, c = ignitionRatio * escapeCalibration * placement: the observed over the expected ignitions; the observed escapes over those expected from the observed ignitions (sum(ignitions * q): the escape model's calibration where ignitions happened); and qObserved / qModel, the mean q where ignitions were observed over the mean q where the model places them. A placement factor above 1 means the ignition model places ignitions where escaping is less likely than where they happened: it is spread too evenly.
